headline: Hackers breach ccTLD registries to mint fake certificates for Google
summary: Attackers compromised domain registries and used the breach to hijack top-level domains and obtain unauthorized HTTPS certificates impersonating Google and other large services. The fake certificates allowed trusted-brand impersonation without triggering normal browser warnings; affected ccTLDs include Ghana, American Samoa, and Sierra Leone.

claims.statement: Hackers compromised ccTLD domain registries and obtained unauthorized certificates for Google and other services.

sources.quote: Compromise of 3 domain registries allows hackers to walk off with unauthorized certs.
Attackers hijacked top-level domains, minted fake security certs for Google and other orgs
Hackers obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for several Google domains and hijacked domains in the country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) for Ghana, American Samoa, and Sierra Leone

claims.statement: The fake certificates allowed trusted-brand impersonation without triggering normal browser certificate warnings.
